players.product: cloud compute and AI infrastructure for molecular and biological discovery

contracts.signal: Ginkgo's 10-K: in August 2023 it entered into a five-year strategic cloud and AI partnership with Google Cloud that included minimum annual commitments to purchase cloud hosting services; under it Ginkgo develops large language models running on Google Cloud's Vertex AI platform across genomics, protein function and synthetic biology, and its AI foundational and fine-tuned models (a selection released on its Model API) are powered by the partnership. The original aggregate future purchase commitment was $289 million; an amendment effective October 3, 2025 revised it to $110 million with reset annual commitments from $6.0 million (year 1, starting October 3, 2025) to $38.0 million (year 6), and required a one-time payment of $14.0 million to be released from the original obligations. Ginkgo recognized a contractual liability of $20.9 million in 2025 for a shortfall in purchasing relative to its commitments under the original agreement.
contracts.units: cloud hosting services under minimum annual purchase commitments

players.product: synthetic DNA, proteins, antibody libraries, and characterization data

contracts.signal: Ginkgo's 10-K: it has a four-year supply agreement with Twist, effective April 1, 2022, for the purchase of diverse products including synthetic DNA, which obligated a minimum spend of $58.0 million over the term. An amendment effective April 1, 2025 converts the remaining minimum annual commitments into non-refundable payments creditable against future purchases, with no expiration: $4.0 million paid in April 2025, $5.0 million on April 1, 2026 and $6.0 million on April 1, 2027. A contractual loss of $8.7 million was recorded in 2025.
contracts.value: $58.0 million minimum spend over four years (original agreement)

contracts.signal: Ginkgo's 10-K names its partnership with Bayer Crop Sciences, developing biological solutions for nitrogen fixation in non-legume crops to reduce reliance on industrial fertilizers, as a flagship example of its agricultural R&D services.

quarterly_data.signal: Remaining performance obligations (excluding cost-plus contracts under the practical expedient) were $158.6 million as of December 31, 2025, versus $85.8 million a year earlier; approximately $23.0 million is expected to be recognized as revenue in 2026. Cell Engineering revenue by industry in 2025: pharmaceutical and biotechnology 35%, agriculture 28%, government and defense 23%, industrial and environment 5%, consumer and technology 5%, food and nutrition 4% (food and nutrition was 32% in 2024).
